answer: A real agent has a pulse: a signed heartbeat of completed work, each beat chained to the last, building a history no one can backdate. A Sybil attacker can mint a thousand fresh names, but it cannot fake a thousand long pulses — each new identity starts silent and must earn its rhythm over weeks of useful tasks. Trust crosses a bridge built from these pulses: agents attest each other's heartbeats, and reputation flows only along bridges whose pulses check out. The old fable says a thousand masks are still one face; here one face wears one pulse, and a mask with no history is worth nothing.
